name: Bikini Wax EPS
funding: Artist cooperative collective dues, grassroots patrons; 0% state co-optation or corporate sponsorship.

name: Bildmuseet
funding: University museum of Umeå University, funded by the Swedish state.
records_note: It posts annual reports 2012 to 2022; parent Umeå University posts annual reports 2024 and 2025 and lists its board; no funder list.

name: Birmingham Museum of Art
funding: City-owned; endowment trust spent $1.3M (FY2025); top corporate circle is Alabama Power, PNC, Protective, Regions and EBSCO.
watch: Alabama Power, a Founders Circle sponsor, runs coal plants including Miller, the largest US CO2 emitter as of 2021. Drummond is not on the list.
records_note: Annual reports with financial statements for selected years 2005-06 to 2023-24 on its site, an undated corporate sponsor list, and the 2026-27 board listed.

name: Bishkek School of Contemporary Art (BiSCA)
funding: Founders built its online school at no cost, per 24.kg (2020). Asia Art Archive is a partner on Mobile Library: Kyrgyzstan, April 2025 to June 2026. No funder list found.
watch: Co-founder Bermet Borubaeva also co-founded the TRASH environmental art festival in 2009 and co-curates it.
records_note: No BiSCA website was found; searches show only Asia Art Archive as a project partner, with no reports, accounts, donor list or board.

name: Bishop Museum (Bernice Pauahi Bishop Museum)
funding: 2023 revenue US$21.5M (IRS 990), from state and federal agencies, Hawai'i foundations such as Kamehameha Schools, and Hawai'i corporate sponsors.
watch: Hawai'i's state museum of natural and cultural history, founded in memory of Princess Bernice Pauahi Bishop.
records_note: The museum posts annual reports for 2020 to 2025, audited statements and Form 990s, named corporate and foundation donors, and its board of directors.

name: Blanton Museum of Art
funding: Part of the University of Texas at Austin. Leadership Board chaired by Elle Moody. 2024-25 gifts of $100,000+ came from the Scurlock Foundation, Moody Foundation, Blanton family members and others.
watch: Scurlock Foundation money comes from Eddy Scurlock's oil fortune. Namesake Jack Blanton ran Scurlock Oil, and family members sit on the Leadership Board.
records_note: Its 2025 impact report names donors of $5,000 or more for 2024-25 and lists its leadership board; only an operating budget is given, no accounts.

name: blaxTARLINES KUMASI
funding: Art network and incubator tied to the KNUST painting and sculpture department in Kumasi.
watch: Ranked 69 in ArtReview's 2025 Power 100 and invited to the 2026 Venice Biennale main exhibition.
records_note: No blaxTARLINES website was found; Wikipedia lists none and no source names a funder, report, accounts or board.

name: Bloc Projects
funding: Arts Council England National Portfolio, Sheffield City Council; artist-led registered charity.
watch: Artist-led project space in a former industrial courtyard in Sheffield; commissions emerging artists and critical research.

name: Boise Art Museum
funding: Expenses $1.7M (FY2026); E.A. Michelson Philanthropy, Steiner and Cunningham foundations, NEA and Idaho Commission on the Arts, with local firms.
watch: Idaho Power, which sponsors the seniors programme, still owns a coal-plant share (13% coal in 2023). Odom Corporation is an alcohol distributor.
records_note: Annual reports 2011-12 to 2025-26 on its site carry a dated donor list and trustees; Form 990s 2012 to 2024 are on ProPublica.

name: Bonner Kunstverein
funding: Project funders: Kunststiftung NRW, NRW culture ministry, Kemmler Foundation, Art Explora.
records_note: No annual report, accounts or funder roster; the about page lists the ten-person Vorstand, and exhibition pages credit funders such as Stadt Bonn per show.

name: Bonniers Konsthall
records_note: No records of its own; parent Bonnier posts annual reviews 2015 to 2025, accounts 2016 to 2025 and its board; the konsthall lists no funders.

name: Britto Arts Trust
funding: Triangle Network, Prince Claus Fund, Arts Collaboratory, artist donations; registered non-profit trust.
watch: Bangladesh's first artist-run non-profit collective; organizers of the 54th Venice Biennale Bangladesh pavilion.
